definition: Pervasive means spread through every part of something — present wherever you look within it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word pervasive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know pervasive should be able to work it out from your sentence.

Pervasive means spread through every part of something — present wherever you look within it.
No one at the station ever ordered anyone to stay late.
The pressure was pervasive anyway: it lived in the joking about 'half-days' at six p.m., in the glances at the first coat pulled off its hook, in the schedule that quietly assumed evenings.
New hires absorbed it within a week without being told a thing.
Pervasive is the right word because the pressure has soaked through the whole place — the jokes, the glances, the schedule.
Nothing about it is loud or official; its power is exactly that there is no corner of the station where it isn't.

Pervasive spreads through one whole: a mood pervades an office, damp pervades a cellar, doubt pervades a report.
Its unit-mate ubiquitous turns up everywhere you go — many places, one world.
The smell in a house is pervasive; the coffee chain on every corner is ubiquitous.
And though the word is technically neutral, it keeps low company — bias, odors, and rumors are pervasive more often than joy is.

The research vessel set out in 2019 to map where ocean plastic collects, expecting to find it bunched near ports and shipping lanes.
Instead, the survey found the fibers to be pervasive: they appeared in every one of the 114 samples the crew hauled up.
Water drawn beside a container port carried them, but so did water from mid-ocean gyres a thousand miles from any coast.
Sediment from the deepest trench sampled held fibers; so did surface foam, so did Arctic ice cores.
The team had set out to draw a map of hot spots.
They came home reporting that, for this pollutant, the map had no blank spaces left.
